doc.name: A — knives catalogue, chrome podium, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: damascus chef knife
Category: knives
Shot programme: chrome podium
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a knives catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-hand scale in a chrome podium treatment.

SUBJECT. A damascus chef knife. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Held in a hand that provides scale, hand cropped at the wrist. Shoot on a 50mm anamorphic with 2x squeeze at f/1.8, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a beauty dish above the lens axis with a silver reflector under the chin. Stage the product on or against ribbed fluted glass, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a desaturated Nordic palette with cold blue shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
